strengths: Novel and well-motivated problem formulations (RAA and RR) addressing important safety-critical RL objectives
Solid theoretical contributions with clean decomposition theorems reducing dual-objective problems to simpler reach/avoid/reach-avoid subproblems
Rigorous mathematical framework with comprehensive proofs; Theorem 3 elegantly shows necessity and sufficiency of state augmentation
Clear intuition provided through illustrative examples (Figure 2) for why state augmentation is required
Practical algorithm (DO-HJ-PPO) naturally derived from theory with reasonable engineering choices
weaknesses: Severely insufficient experimental validation: only 1,000 trajectories per task with no error bars, confidence intervals, or statistical significance testing; results cannot be considered reliable
Weak and unfair baseline comparisons: CPPO variants appear intentionally weak; missing comparisons to recent safe RL, multi-objective Pareto methods, and goal-conditioned RL approaches

Critical absence of ablation studies on claimed key design choices: no ablation on coupled resets (claimed as significantly important), simultaneous vs. sequential optimization, or discount factor sensitivity

Significant gap between theory and practice: deterministic dynamics assumed in theory but stochastic SRABE used in practice; approximation error analysis missing; modified dynamics f' with absorbing states appears ad-hoc
Scalability and generalization concerns: state augmentation approach unclear for high-dimensional spaces; no discussion of 3+ objectives; all experiments on simple, low-dimensional domains

Incomplete presentation: Hamilton-Jacobi connection mentioned prominently but underdeveloped; practical applicability and when to use RAA/RR over alternatives not addressed; design choices lack clear motivation
Reproducibility issues: no code availability mentioned, coupled resets implementation unclear, exact nature of state initialization during learning not specified

strengths: Rigorous theoretical contributions with elegant decomposition results (Theorems 1-3) showing RAA and RR problems reduce to compositions of simpler HJ-RL problems
Well-motivated problem formulations addressing natural scenarios in safe RL: safe arrival with post-arrival safety, and multi-target achievement
Comprehensive experimental evaluation across 4 environments with diverse baselines (Lagrangian, HJ-RL, STL/LTL, MORL) showing DOHJ-PPO consistently ranks first or second
Strong and consistent empirical results with clear performance metrics (success rate, partial success, achievement time) and ablation studies
Thoughtful appendix addressing theoretical-practical distinctions and explaining why temporal logic decompositions don't apply to HJ value functions
Practical algorithm (DOHJ-PPO) with well-motivated design choices such as coupled resets for concurrent training of decomposed objectives
weaknesses: Incremental novelty: Extension from {R, A, RA} to {RAA, RR} is somewhat straightforward once state augmentation is introduced; conceptual advance over existing HJ-RL work is moderate

Significant theory-practice gap: DOHJ-PPO relies on SRABE approximation that exchanges expectation and extrema operators (which don't commute), with no formal convergence guarantees or approximation bounds provided

Fundamental limitation from state augmentation requirement: Non-augmented policies cannot solve these problems optimally, requiring memory which limits applicability and increases state dimensionality

Incomplete stochastic dynamics handling: Section 8.3 shows substantial performance degradation with high noise; SRABE validity under stochasticity lacks theoretical justification; real-world applicability is questionable
Questionable baseline fairness: CPPO reformulations appear ad-hoc, STL baselines improvised without justification, unclear if baselines received equal tuning despite claims of 'little to no tuning'
Limited experimental scope: All tasks involve simple spatial targets; no demonstration on problems where augmented state information is unavailable; insufficient failure mode analysis
Algorithm complexity not fully justified: Multiple critic/actor networks increase implementation burden; crucial coupled resets mechanism lacks theoretical justification beyond empirical observation
Presentation could be improved: Dense notation with heavy superscripts; distinction between theoretical (augmented) and practical formulations unclear upfront
